title: Distributed Vector Database with HNSW Index & Reciprocal Rank Fusion
subtitle: Hierarchical Navigable Small World Graphs, DiskANN (Vamana) and Dense/Sparse RRF Merging
problem_statement: An AI semantic search engine indexing 500 million embeddings (1536 dimensions) suffers high query latency (P99 > 850ms) and prohibitive RAM costs ($45,000/month for in-memory HNSW). The system must maintain 95%+ recall while slashing RAM by 70% using Product Quantization and hybrid BM25 + dense RRF.

faded_bug.description: Unquantized FP32 embeddings in RAM exhaust node memory at 500M vectors.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
+ // Enable Product Quantization (IVF-PQ) or Scalar Quantization (SQ8) with DiskANN (Vamana graph)
+ self.dense.enable_diskann_with_pq(code_bytes=32);

invariants.description: End-to-end vector search P99 latency must remain under 30ms with Recall@10 > 95%.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the hierarchical layers in an HNSW graph. How does the beam search parameter `efSearch` balance recall vs query latency?
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: How does Product Quantization (PQ) compress 1536-dimensional vectors into 64 bytes? What is the mathematical origin of quantization distortion?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A user searches with metadata filtering: `category = 'finance' AND date > 2026-01-01`. Why does post-filtering cause recall collapse when the filter matches <1% of documents?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Compare in-memory HNSW with NVMe SSD-based DiskANN (Vamana). How does asynchronous I/O (`io_uring`) keep P99 latency under 15ms?

counter_probes.counter_question: If your HNSW search returns the top 100 nearest neighbors, but your metadata post-filter matches only 0.5% of total documents, how many results will the user receive?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Zero or near-zero results (recall collapse). Filtered vector search must use Single-Stage Iterative HNSW or Pre-filtered inverted lists to traverse only nodes that satisfy the predicate.
